title: Three sibling parity tools carry three root-resolution contracts, deciding fixture-drivability by accident
body:
Three sibling parity tools carry three different root-resolution contracts, and the divergence decides which of them can be driven against a fixture at all:

- `view_skew_check.sh:78` -- `ROOT="${ROOT:-...}"`: honours an inherited `ROOT`.
- `thread_view_skew_check.sh:70` -- `ROOT="$(...)"`: silently DISCARDS an inherited `ROOT` (its own roster row already records the consequence: "an env-var drive silently runs against the real tree and reports a success that measured nothing, which is how the first attempt at this evidence went").
- `guard_home_check.sh` -- `ROOT="${PROJECT_ROOT:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)}"`: honours a DIFFERENT variable.

Flagged by intent-ic (two of the three, from memory of the contracts, without reading mid-write diffs); confirmed with exact line numbers and widened to the third by intent-dc while closing 0112/0113 in the same files (2026-08-28, family commits `69ea2657`/`a12147c1`). dc deliberately did NOT fold a fix into 0112 -- a new defect outside an assigned family, correctly routed instead of lane-widened.

**Why it matters beyond tidiness:** a tool that discards the env var cannot be pointed at a fixture, so its arms can only be driven against the real tree -- the exact blindness dc hit the same day when `int hooks` refused to be pointed anywhere but its own tree, and the mechanism behind thread_view_skew's recorded first-attempt failure. A contributor who learns one contract from one sibling silently measures the wrong tree in the next.

**Fix shape:** one contract for the family (honour an explicit override, resolve by git toplevel otherwise -- and ONE variable name), stated once; each tool's fixture-drivability then follows from the shared contract instead of varying by author.
